subject: How can I run a runtime name of a file in a Shiny server if the name is calculated before hand.

messages.author: a269b5685283b25b
messages.subject: How can I run a runtime name of a file in a Shiny server if the name is calculated before hand.
parts:
Hello,

This is a small question. How can I run:

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  source(my_source_file_name1, local=TRUE)
  source(my_source_file_name2, local=TRUE)
  source(my_source_file_name3, local=TRUE)
  # and so on...
}

...without having to specify each file name? It works if I specify it manually, but I want to calculate the paths from a text file before hand at runtime.

I've currently broken down my app's server files into about 10 or 11 different files. I have a text file which contains their names; I'm able to load the UI files and run an installation script to run the files based on the paths I calculate at runtime, but I cannot do this for the server function. Should I make a function that returns another function with the source file names parameterized on the server function generator function? 

Sincerely,
Austin

messages.subject: Re: How can I run a runtime name of a file in a Shiny server if the name is calculated before hand.
parts: Instead of local=TRUE, try local=environment(). But even better, take a look at modules. http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html
